plan.title: BLOCKER: bug(codex): occupancy lease self-denies direct writes after session:start

narratives.Description: BLOCKER: bug(codex): occupancy lease self-denies direct writes after session:start
narratives.Overview:
## Summary

On Codex, Claude Code, and other hosts that run each hook in a fresh process, a successful `deft session:start` can claim a worktree occupancy lease but later direct-write hooks do not inherit `DEFT_SESSION_ID` from that completed shell process.

The same host conversation is then denied as though it were a competing session:

```text
Directive denied apply_patch: Worktree occupied by session <the session just minted>
```

This is distinct from stale heartbeats (#3599), missing ordinary release (#3604), and never-claimed sessions (#3729). It occurs immediately while the lease is live because the host hook cannot bind itself to the lease that its conversation just claimed.

mechanism-shaped: true

## Reproduction

1. In Codex or Claude Code, run `deft session:start` in a consumer repository.
2. Run `deft verify:session-ritual -- --tier=gated`.
3. Invoke the host's direct-write tool (`apply_patch`, `Write`, or `Edit`).
4. Directive rejects the write because the new hook process has no matching `DEFT_SESSION_ID`.
5. Exporting the variable inside the earlier shell invocation does not help. That child process cannot mutate the host environment for later tool calls.

The same defect affects later `session:start --rearm`, `session:ready`, confirmed steal, release/end, and `swarm:launch` paths when they independently mint or resolve identity.

## Implementation evidence

`evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` accepts only an explicit session ID or `env.DEFT_SESSION_ID`. The dispatcher currently discards stable host identity from the hook payload before occupancy evaluation.

Codex, Claude Code, and Cursor document stable session or conversation identifiers in hook input. They also document `PreToolUse` input rewriting. This permits a claim-time bridge without a persisted host-to-lease map: an exact Directive lifecycle command can receive a canonical explicit `--session-id`, and later direct-write hooks can derive the same identity from their host payload.

## Actual behavior

The owner of a freshly claimed lease cannot use direct-write tools. Existing recovery text can make the state worse: `session:start --steal` currently mutates during preview and then attempts a second steal, while `session:ready` can resolve different IDs across preview, nested start, and final claim.

## Locked implementation contract

The approved target is **cooperative host-session or conversation exclusion**, not security-grade authorization against another same-user process. Host identity is forgeable at the local hook boundary, but normal host-delivered events must distinguish concurrent conversations.

Use a namespaced and versioned canonical owner ID derived from the provider payload, such as:

```text
host:<provider>:v1:<base64url(raw-host-session-id)>
```

- Codex uses `session_id`; the owner includes the parent session and its subagents.
- Claude Code uses `session_id`; `agent_id` does not replace the session-family key.
- Cursor uses `conversation_id`; conflicting simultaneous identity fields fail closed. Parent/subagent behavior must be verified before a stronger family claim is documented.
- Grok preserves the existing explicit/environment path until it has a documented payload identity.
- Manual or non-host CLI callers continue to use explicit `--session-id` or `DEFT_SESSION_ID`.

For an active occupancy lease, the canonical host owner, live lease owner, and owner from the exact ritual state evaluated by gated verification must agree. Ritual state validates readiness and alignment; it must not manufacture actor identity for an unpinned write hook. Missing, malformed, or conflicting host identity fails closed while the lease is live.

The claim-time rewrite is limited to exact, simple, canonical Directive lifecycle commands. Compound commands, redirections, aliases, and ambiguous wrappers are not rewritten because the required host `allow` response may also approve the command. Independent hook and host policy denials must continue to win.

The detailed approved design and source findings are recorded in the [reevaluation amendment](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3611#issuecomment-5425117914). It supersedes the [original plan](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3611#issuecomment-5424890479).

## Acceptance criteria

1. A standard host-mediated mutation ceremony claims the lease and writes ritual state with the same canonical host session ID without relying on inherited `DEFT_SESSION_ID`.
2. A later direct-write hook from the same host session is allowed with no environment ID.
3. A different concurrent host conversation is denied even when both can read the same worktree ritual state.
4. Missing, malformed, or conflicting payload identity fails closed when a live lease exists.
5. The exact verified ritual owner, live lease owner, and canonical host owner must agree. A mismatch never allows a write.
6. No persisted host-to-lease map, credential artifact, occupancy-derived caller identity, or schema migration is introduced.
7. Rearm, ready, release/end, confirmed steal, and swarm launch carry one resolved identity through their complete state machines.
8. Confirmed `session:start --steal` steals once and establishes matching lease and ritual state. Bare steal reports explicit mismatch recovery.
9. Real child-process tests cover claim and later hook lifetimes with host-shaped payloads and parse the rendered verdict.
10. Existing expiry, locking/fencing, read-only, scope, runtime, assist-scratch, and separately tracked spawn behavior is preserved.

## Required regression matrix

- Payload identity agrees or conflicts with explicit/environment identity.
- Codex parent and subagent events share the intended session-family owner.
- Claude session plus `agent_id` still uses the session-family owner.
- Cursor concurrent conversations differ; parent/subagent behavior is live-verified.
- Exact lifecycle commands are rewritten; compound or ambiguous commands are refused.
- An independent policy denial is not bypassed by input rewriting.
- A matching stale ritual reports `ritual-not-ready`, not `occupancy-occupied`.
- A verified-state ownership transition from A to B cannot let old hook A proceed.
- Cold `session:ready` does not mint independent preview, start, and final IDs.
- Confirmed steal occurs once and leaves matching lease and ritual state.
- Bare steal yields mismatch denial with deterministic recovery.
- `swarm:launch`, release, and session end reuse canonical A and reject foreign B.
- POSIX and Windows child invocation uses explicit arguments rather than shell environment-prefix syntax.

## Boundaries

- #3599 remains the immediate follow-up for live heartbeats.
- #3729, #3742, #3754, and #3755 remain separate issues.
- This change does not turn local files or hook JSON into an authentication boundary.
- No occupancy schema or lease-TTL migration is included.

## Environment

- Initially reported with `@deftai/directive` 0.105.0 on Codex desktop and macOS.
- Independently reproduced with 0.106.0 on Claude Code desktop and Windows 11.

## Related but not duplicate

- #3433 - occupancy feature
- #3599 - active leases never heartbeat
- #3604 - ordinary sessions never release
- #3613 - coordination-defect tracker
- #3729 - never-claimed sessions are not gated
- #3742 - missing or drifted hooks
- #3754 - lifecycle composition gap
- #3755 - spawn occupancy bypass

---

## Issue comment thread

_The issue body is the original write-up; maintainer comments below may supersede it. Read the full thread before building a dispatch envelope (#2143)._

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-21T20:34:34Z)

Grouped under tracker #3613 (multi-agent coordination defects) as the **identity** dimension. Your framing is right — this is distinct from #3599 and #3604, and together the four make a complete set of gaps in one model: liveness (#3599), lifecycle (#3604), keyspace (#3607, issue threads have no interlock at all), and identity (this one).

**A dependency worth recording: this issue blocks #3599.** Both defects live in the same function, `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:394`):

```ts
const incoming = input.sessionId?.trim() || (input.env ?? process.env).DEFT_SESSION_ID?.trim() || "";
if (incoming.length > 0 && incoming === live.sessionId) {
  return { allow: true, message: null, occupant: live };   // <- #3599's heartbeat belongs here
}
return { allow: false, ... };                              // <- your self-deny lands here
```

#3599's proposed fix is to re-stamp `heartbeat_at` on the same-session branch. But that branch is only reached when `incoming === live.sessionId` — precisely what this issue says cannot happen when the hook process has no `DEFT_SESSION_ID`. **So the heartbeat fix is unreachable until identity binding works.** Sequencing #3599 first would produce a change that appears correct and never executes on the affected hosts.

Corollary for whoever implements: a session that cannot identify itself also cannot keep its own lease alive, which means on those hosts the lease is guaranteed to expire and become a steal candidate — the mechanism behind the incident in #3599. Identity is the root of that chain, not a sibling of it.

### Comment by @ZaenKai (2026-08-23T02:52:16Z)

Confirming this on a second host and a second platform, at 0.106.0 — the defect is not Codex-specific.

**Environment:** Claude Code (desktop), Windows 11 Pro 26200, `@deftai/directive` 0.106.0, engine and content 0.106.0, consumer deposit in hybrid mode.

**Same shape.** A mutation `deft session:start` claims the lease, then every `Write` / `Edit` / `MultiEdit` is denied:

```text
Directive denied Write: Worktree occupied by session c079c244-… (intent=mutation, heartbeat 32s ago).
```

The heartbeat is seconds old and the lease is the one this very agent just minted. As reported here, the hook is spawned by the host with the ambient environment, which carries no `DEFT_SESSION_ID`, so `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` cannot recognise the owner. Exporting the variable in a shell does not help — the shell is a different process from the hook.

Three things this run adds to the report:

**1. `occupancy:steal --confirm` does not recover it.** The obvious reading of the remediation text is that stealing the lease into your own identity restores write access. It does not. Stealing it into the host session id — the id in the agent's own working paths — reports success and changes nothing:

```console
$ DEFT_SESSION_ID=86c96a4d-… deft occupancy:steal --confirm --occupant c079c244-…
occupancy stolen from c079c244-…; writer is now session 86c96a4d-…
```

and the very next `Write` is denied again, now naming `86c96a4d-…` as the occupant. The gate reads `DEFT_SESSION_ID` **from the hook's process environment**, and no value written into the lease file can change what that process inherits. So every remediation the message offers except "use another worktree" is unreachable from inside the session that is blocked.

**2. Deleting the lease file is a clean recovery, and costs nothing.** `rm -f .deft/occupancy.json` restores writes immediately, and `deft verify:session-ritual -- --tier=gated` still reports fresh afterwards — the ritual state is independent of the lease, so nothing else has to be re-armed. That is a better recovery than importing the internal `releaseOccupancy` API, and worth naming in the remediation text even before the binding is fixed.

**3. Bash writes are unaffected, which is what hides it.** The `PreToolUse` matcher covers the direct-write tools; a shell heredoc or `sed` writing the same file passes. An agent that happens to do its file work through the shell will never see the gate, and one that uses the host's edit tools is stopped on its first write. On this run the trap only surfaced when the agent switched from shell edits to `Write` partway through a session — same session, same lease, same second.

**On the acceptance criteria as written:** "Persist a safe host/session binding that later hook events can resolve" is the right shape, but the binding has to be keyed on something the *host* supplies to the hook, not on something the CLI can write down. Claude Code and Codex both pass a host session id in the hook payload; neither passes `DEFT_SESSION_ID`. If the payload's session identity were accepted as an ownership proof alongside the env var, both hosts would be covered without either of them changing.

Worth adding a Claude Code / win32 regression fixture beside the Codex one — the two hosts fail identically, which suggests the fixture should be "any host that spawns hooks with an ambient environment" rather than a per-host case.


### Comment by @ZaenKai (2026-08-23T12:00:56Z)

One more door into this, found on a long session at 0.106.0 — and it is the framework's own remediation text that opens it.

**The report above names cold `deft session:start` as what claims the lease. `session:start --rearm` and `deft session:ready` claim it too**, and those are the two commands the *session-ritual staleness* refusal tells you to run.

## The loop

A single agent session ran past `plan.policy.sessionRitualStalenessHours` (default 4) while doing planning and then implementation. The next `Edit` was refused — not by the occupancy gate, by the staleness gate:

```text
Directive denied Edit: session ritual state is stale (older than 4h).
Run `deft session:start --rearm` to re-arm (or `deft session:start` for a full cold ceremony).
Recovery: run deft session:ready (one-shot), or deft session:start --rearm ...,
then deft verify:session-ritual -- --tier=gated.
```

Following it exactly:

```console
$ deft session:start --rearm
[deft session] ceremony rearm 2792ms
[deft] session ritual recorded at ...\.deft\ritual-state.json
```

and the next `Edit` is refused again, now by *this* issue:

```text
Directive denied Edit: Worktree occupied by session b9b8b671-… (intent=mutation, heartbeat 0s ago).
```

So gate A's documented recovery triggers gate B. `rm -f .deft/occupancy.json` clears it, as established above, and `deft verify:session-ritual -- --tier=gated` still reports fresh afterwards — same clean recovery, no re-arm needed.

## Why this is worth more than a footnote

The first encounter with this defect is a surprise. **This one is on a timer.** Any session long enough to cross the staleness window hits it, and hits it again every window after — and the agent is being *told* to run the command that breaks it, by the framework, at the exact moment it is trying to comply with another framework gate. An agent that has not read this issue will follow the remediation text, get denied, follow it again, and conclude the tool is broken rather than that two gates disagree.

It also means the practical blast radius is wider than "you ran `session:start`". A session that never runs a mutation ceremony at all still lands here eventually, because staleness arrives on its own.

## Suggested shapes, in order of how cheap they look from outside

1. **Do not claim a lease on `--rearm` or `session:ready`.** Re-arming ritual freshness and claiming worktree occupancy are different concerns; the staleness recovery only needs the first.
2. **Name the lease in the staleness remediation text**, so an agent following it knows what is about to happen and that `rm -f .deft/occupancy.json` is the exit — cheap, and useful even after the binding is fixed.
3. The binding fix already discussed above, which makes both moot.

**Environment:** Claude Code (desktop), Windows 11 Pro 26200, `@deftai/directive` 0.106.0, engine/content/pin aligned, hybrid consumer deposit, git worktree.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-26T04:43:11Z)

model: gpt-5.6-sol-medium
role: critic

Refutation result: the target does **not** survive as an absolute process-identity claim. It survives only as a cooperative host-session routing claim, which is narrower than “a different task or process must remain denied.”

## Replayable bearer binding
class: blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** At dispatch SHA `c784755f08773b8e861567d8df7780aea310cc57`, the existing lease is ordinary project-readable JSON: `readOccupancy` parses it from disk, and the serialized payload contains `session_id`, `host`, and `address` (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:121-135`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:511-533`). The write gate proves ownership by equality with a caller-supplied string, not by provenance of that string (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:402-422`). The hook executable likewise accepts arbitrary JSON from stdin and forwards it into `decideHook`; there is no authenticated host channel at that boundary (`packages/cli/src/hook-dispatch.ts:193-210`).

I measured three fresh child processes against a lease in an OS-temp worktree. An unbound child was denied (`pid 156420`, `allow:false`); a different child replaying `DEFT_SESSION_ID=owner-token` was allowed (`pid 35204`, `allow:true`); and a third child read `owner-token` from the on-disk lease and supplied it explicitly (`pid 68800`, `allow:true`). The targeted occupancy suite also passed 22/22, so this is the specified bearer-token behavior rather than a failing baseline.

**Failure mode.** A second process running as the same user can read a project-scoped host/session binding and replay every value it contains. Moving the equality key from `occupancy.json` to another file does not make it process identity. The same process can also invoke `deft-hook` with forged stdin. File ACL hardening beyond normal same-user project permissions is unverified, but it would not distinguish two processes running as that user.

**Disposition consequence.** The design cannot promise denial of an arbitrary different same-host process using only persisted binding plus hook JSON. Either narrow the contract to non-Byzantine/cooperating host sessions—the source already states that concurrency model (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:9-14`)—or add a trust boundary that the competing process cannot replay, such as a broker with OS-authenticated IPC/peer credentials. A second project file is not that boundary.

## Codex session identity is not task identity
class: blocks-the-design

**Evidence.** Codex’s official hook schema says `session_id` is the current session ID and that subagent hooks use the parent session ID; `PreToolUse` adds `turn_id`, but not a stable per-agent ID: https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks#common-input-fields and https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks#pretooluse. Live payload confirmation on the reporter’s Codex version is unverified. In this tree, the provider-neutral parser preserves the JSON object, but occupancy evaluation receives only `env`, so payload identity is currently discarded (`packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:921-940`). I measured a Codex-shaped payload carrying `session_id=host-session-1`: payload-only produced `deny/occupancy-occupied`, while the same event with that value copied into `DEFT_SESSION_ID` produced `allow/write-ready`.

**Failure mode.** If the owner is one task/agent rather than the whole Codex session family, a parent and its subagent can present the same `session_id`. Binding that value distinguishes sessions, not processes or tasks. `turn_id` cannot repair this: it changes by turn, so it is not a durable owner key.

**Disposition consequence.** Define the lease owner granularity before binding. “Codex session and all of its subagents” is implementable as cooperative session ownership. “The one host task/process that claimed” is not implementable from the documented Codex `PreToolUse` identity surface. Host-specific stronger keys may be used where present, but they cannot justify a cross-host task-identity claim.

## Binding lifetime needs independent revocation
class: sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** Occupancy expires after 20 minutes without a heartbeat (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:28-29`, `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:87-93`), while the proposed binding has no stated expiry or generation. Current Codex deposit installs `SessionStart` and `PreToolUse` handlers but no `SessionEnd` handler (`.codex/hooks.json:3-55`). Codex now documents `SessionEnd`, but its delivery and behavior on crash are unverified for the affected host/version.

**Failure mode.** A task exits while its binding remains. A resumed, duplicated, or replaying caller with the old host ID can continue to satisfy the binding until some separate cleanup occurs; if the binding survives lease replacement, it can incorrectly authorize a later generation.

**Disposition consequence.** Bind to an occupancy generation/nonce, expire the binding no later than the lease, remove it on supported end hooks, and make lease replacement invalidate prior bindings atomically. Crash/timeout remains the fallback. Resume semantics must say whether reuse of the same host session ID intentionally resumes ownership.

## Separate binding can satisfy the no-fallback criterion
class: sharpens-framing

**Evidence.** The current gate already denies an unbound caller despite being able to read the live occupancy record (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:411-422`), and its regression explicitly checks both “unbound denies” and “matching explicit identity allows” (`packages/core/src/session/occupancy.test.ts:160-169`). Therefore the acceptance criterion not to treat the live occupancy file itself as proof is mechanically satisfiable: require a host key, resolve it through a distinct binding, then compare the resulting lease generation.

**Failure mode.** Treating this as a security proof would overclaim. It prevents accidental self-denial and accidental cross-session admission among honest host events; it does not stop the replay in “Replayable bearer binding.”

**Disposition consequence.** Keep the criterion, but state its boundary: it is a fail-closed routing rule for unbound cooperative callers, not authentication against another same-user process.

## PID ancestry is not a portable substitute
class: footnote

The hook deposits execute a command for each matched event (`.codex/hooks.json:14-53`), so the hook child PID is necessarily per-invocation rather than durable. Stable/exclusive parent PID, process start-time, job-object, or equivalent host handles across Codex, Claude, Cursor, and Grok are unverified. I would reject PID-only binding unless each supported host demonstrates an exclusive stable parent handle and the verifier binds PID plus creation identity to defeat reuse.

**Road not taken and flip condition.** I rejected “persist a random secret beside the lease” because it is still readable/replayable by the process class the claim says must be denied. The strongest case for the proposal is the source’s existing non-Byzantine local-filesystem model: under honest host delivery, stable host session IDs do distinguish separate sessions and solve the reported self-denial. My blocking verdict would flip if the claim is narrowed to that cooperative boundary, or if measurement shows an authenticated host-to-hook channel/OS credential that a second same-user process cannot forge or replay.


### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-08-26T04:43:50Z)

model: claude-opus-5-thinking-high-fast
role: critic

**Verdict on the refutation target: broken.** A persisted binding distinguishes *knowledge of a string* from *ignorance of that string*. On the reporting platform that string is published on disk in at least four places at mode `0644`, and I recovered a live one from a directory listing alone, without reading any file, in 99 ms. The premise survives only after a rewording that deletes the word "persisted" -- Finding 5.

**Method.** All cites re-opened at `c784755f`. I re-derived the write-back's anchors rather than copying them, ran `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` against a throwaway fixture root under `%TEMP%` (never this repo), ran an offline id-recovery probe against the `.deft/session-binds` listing, walked the live process ancestry of a host-spawned shell, and read the live identity environment. Nothing in this repository was modified; the lease was not claimed, released, or stolen.

---

## The credential is a published string

`blocks-the-design`

The gate's entire input is a project root and an environment. `packages/core/src/hooks/dispatcher.ts:921-923` calls `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate(projectRoot, { env: environ })`, where `environ` is `input.environ ?? process.env` (`dispatcher.ts:845`); `packages/cli/src/hook-dispatch.ts:200-209` builds the dispatch input from stdin and passes no `environ` at all. `packages/core/src/session/occupancy.ts:413-415` then admits on string equality alone.

Measured against a temp fixture holding a fresh lease:

```text
owner hook, ambient env (no DEFT_SESSION_ID): allow=false
stranger process naming recovered id:         allow=true
genuinely different session id:               allow=false
fallback: env<-occupancy.json own session_id: allow=true
```

Row 4 is precisely what a disk-resolved binding computes. The same id sits in cleartext in four places: `.deft/occupancy.json` (`session_id`), `.deft/ritual-state.json` (`session_id` -- measured `93a5f27b-7a67-46ed-99ff-d6fcafd6e598`, identical to the id in the denial quoted in the write-back), `.deft/session-binds/<id>.json` (`sessionId`), and `.deft/swarm-launch-occupancy/*.json` (`occupancy_session_id` -- measured in `plan-3596-through-merge.json`). All four are written through `writeNoFollow` (`packages/core/src/fs/contained-write.ts:368`), which opens at `0o644` -- world-readable on macOS, the platform in the report.

Failure mode: a second agent task in the same worktree reads any of those files, exports the id, and writes. This needs no adversary. Every agent already has repository read, so the routine multi-agent case is the exploit.

Disposition consequence: AC1 as written cannot bind as an authorization mechanism. It is an availability fix wearing an authorization label, and the lean must say which of the two it is buying.

## A directory listing is enough

`blocks-the-design`

`safeSessionFileName` (`packages/core/src/freshness/bind.ts:44-72`) builds the record name from the first 32 characters of the session id plus a 24-hex-character SHA-256 prefix of the full id. A UUID is 36 characters, so exactly 4 hex characters are unknown -- 65,536 candidates, and the filename ships the oracle to check them against.

Measured, reading no file contents, only `readdir`:

```text
filename=93a5f27b-7a67-46ed-99ff-d6fcafd6-072b3da95a88a848d12c5ade.json
leaked_prefix=93a5f27b-7a67-46ed-99ff-d6fcafd6  (32 chars)
recovered_session_id=93a5f27b-7a67-46ed-99ff-d6fcafd6e598
candidates_tried=58777   elapsed_ms=99.4
```

Failure mode: read permission on the *directory* is sufficient. Tightening file contents or per-file ACLs does not close this.

Disposition consequence: any remedy that stores per-session records under an id-derived filename inherits the leak. AC1 must forbid id-derived names, or place the store outside the repository, or the hardening is cosmetic.

## The occupancy schema already has host and address, and they are dead

`blocks-the-design`

`OccupancyRecord` already carries `host` and `address` (`occupancy.ts:42-43`). They are populated by `occupancyHost` / `occupancyAddress` (`occupancy.ts:465-473`) from `DEFT_AGENT_ID` and `DEFT_SESSION_NAME`, defaulting to `"none"`; they are parsed back at `occupancy.ts:503-504`; and `evaluateOccupancyWriteGate` (`occupancy.ts:402-423`) never reads them.

Measured in this live host-spawned process on a reproducing host: `DEFT_AGENT_ID`, `DEFT_SESSION_NAME`, and `DEFT_SESSION_ID` are all empty. So every occupancy record this host writes has `host="none"`, `address="none"`.

Failure mode: the storage half of the requested binding already shipped, and it is empty for exactly the reason the issue reports -- it is sourced from the environment, and the environment is what the host does not propagate.

Disposition consequence: the lean must state why populating and checking these two existing fields is not the fix. If it is the fix, #3611 is a wiring change, not a new mechanism, and the AC set should say so.

## #3117 already built this binding, and its own contract concedes the point

`blocks-the-design`

Inventory before proposing new mechanism. `packages/core/src/freshness/bind.ts:8-9` states: multi-agent hosts MUST pass a stable host session identity "so one session cannot certify another as current." But `readBoundGeneration` (`bind.ts:174-177`) verifies only that the caller *named* an id matching the record. The two pin channels the framework documents are `DEFT_SESSION_ID` and `--session-id` (`content/docs/freshness-contract.md:42-52`) -- the two channels this issue reports as unavailable inside a hook. And `packages/core/src/run-summary/session-id.ts:59-89` already implements the exact env-then-ritual-state fallback chain #3611 proposes, as a resolution order with a mint at the end.

Failure mode: adopting the #3117 shape for occupancy imports its threat model wholesale, including the part its own header comment states as a requirement it cannot enforce.

Disposition consequence: the lean must say how an occupancy binding differs from the #3117 binding. If it does not differ, #3611 extends a mechanism that already fails the property the AC demands.

## AC 2 is not satisfiable at the current call site

`blocks-the-design`

AC2 reads: "Do not treat the live occupancy file itself as proof that an unbound caller owns the lease." The gate's total input is a project root plus an environment (`dispatcher.ts:921-923`). Every binding it could resolve is therefore another file under the same `.deft/` directory, with the same `0o644` mode and the same writer set as `occupancy.json`.

This is not hypothetical: the codebase already made this exact move. `occupancy.ts:425` carries the rule "Close-out identity comes from the launch manifest or `DEFT_SESSION_ID` -- never occupancy.json," and the launch manifest turned out to be another bearer file -- measured, `occupancy_session_id` in cleartext.

Failure mode: AC2 is satisfied on paper by introducing any second file, while the property it names is unchanged. It will pass review green.

Disposition consequence: restate AC2 as a constraint on the gate's *inputs* -- add a channel the caller cannot write -- not on which file the gate reads.

## Persistence is the false half; an unforgeable host channel is the true half

`sharpens-framing`

This is the part of the target that survives, and it survives only reworded.

Today no host identity reaches the gate. ### Comment by @dbcall2 (2026-08-26T12:15:57Z)

## Reevaluation amendment — implementation plan changes materially

Reevaluated after [the gap analysis](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3611#issuecomment-5424985570), a fresh `upstream/master` fetch, another source-level lifecycle trace, and current official hook documentation for [Codex](https://developers.openai.com/codex/hooks), [Claude Code](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks), and [Cursor](https://cursor.com/docs/hooks).

`upstream/master` is still `36280b61`; no code change has superseded the earlier analysis. The gap-analysis comment is the only substantive issue-thread event after the original plan.

### Revised verdict

The original plan should **not** use ritual state as the normal write-gate actor identity.

That fallback fixes availability, but `.deft/ritual-state.json` is shared by the worktree. Two concurrent hooks with no strong identity would both be treated as the ritual owner. Calling that result “Codex session-family ownership” was incorrect; it is worktree-ritual ownership and does not preserve the #3433 conversation-exclusion contract.

The revised target is:

> Cooperative host-session/conversation exclusion for normal host-delivered hooks, not security-grade authorization.

Host identity remains forgeable by another same-user process and therefore is not an authentication boundary. However, normal host-delivered events can distinguish concurrent conversations without a persisted host-to-lease map.

### New host-capability finding

All three affected hosts document both a stable conversation/session identifier in hook input and `PreToolUse` input rewriting:

| Host | Cooperative owner key | Granularity | Claim-time bridge available |
|---|---|---|---|
| Codex | `session_id` | Parent session plus subagents | `PreToolUse.updatedInput`; SessionStart context, but no documented SessionStart env output |
| Claude Code | `session_id` | Session family; `agent_id` is additional subagent identity | `PreToolUse.updatedInput`; `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` for later Bash commands |
| Cursor | `conversation_id` / SessionStart `session_id` | Conversation; subagent behavior still needs live confirmation | `preToolUse.updated_input`; SessionStart `env` |

This supplies the missing non-persistent namespace bridge: the hook that observes a canonical Directive lifecycle shell command can inject the host identity as an explicit CLI argument before that command runs. The later direct-write hook derives the same canonical identity from its payload.

The host-specific environment channels are useful corroboration, but they should not be the sole correctness path. Cursor documents fire-and-forget SessionStart behavior, Claude documents `CLAUDE_ENV_FILE` specifically for later Bash commands, and Codex does not document SessionStart environment injection.

## Superseding identity contract

Use a namespaced, versioned, shell-safe owner ID derived from host payload identity, for example:

```text
host:<provider>:v1:<base64url(raw-host-session-id)>
```

For a host-delivered write hook:

1. Extract and validate the provider-specific payload identity.
2. Canonicalize it into the occupancy owner namespace.
3. If explicit/environment identity is also present, require it to agree; conflict fails closed.
4. Require the canonical host identity to match the live occupancy lease.
5. Require the session ID from the **exact ritual state evaluated by verification** to match that same lease/host identity.
6. Missing host identity with a live lease fails closed.

Ritual state validates owner alignment and readiness; it does not manufacture actor identity for an otherwise unpinned normal write.

When no live lease exists, preserve the existing free-worktree behavior. The ritual/actor equality check is needed when occupancy is active, not as a new global authorization gate.

Manual/non-host CLI use remains supported through explicit `--session-id` or `DEFT_SESSION_ID`.

## Revised implementation plan

### 1. Add provider-neutral host identity extraction

Add a strict helper under the hook classify/dispatcher surface:

- Codex: `session_id`.
- Claude: `session_id`; do not use `agent_id` as the cross-host owner key because Codex cannot provide equivalent per-subagent identity.
- Cursor: require a non-empty `conversation_id`; when both `conversation_id` and `session_id` are present, require them to agree.
- Grok: preserve the existing environment path until a documented payload identity is verified; do not silently apply a guessed parser.

Treat malformed, conflicting, or absent values as no host identity. Do not read the occupancy file to fill them in.

### 2. Add the claim-time identity bridge

Add an explicit `--session-id` option and thread it through:

- `session:start` / `--rearm` / confirmed steal.
- `session:ready`.
- `occupancy:steal`.
- `occupancy:release` and therefore `session:end`.
- `swarm:launch`.

Intercept only exact, simple, canonical Directive lifecycle shell commands in `PreToolUse`. Return a rewritten input containing the canonical `--session-id` value:

- Claude/Codex: `hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision="allow"` plus `updatedInput`.
- Cursor: `permission="allow"` plus `updated_input`.

The rewrite must preserve every unchanged tool-input field and existing CLI argument. Encode the ID so it is a single shell-safe token rather than injecting shell-specific environment syntax.

Important safety boundary: returning `allow` with `updatedInput` can auto-approve a command. Therefore:

- Rewrite only the exact lifecycle verbs above.
- Refuse compound, redirected, aliased, or ambiguously parsed commands rather than rewriting them.
- Do not use this path for arbitrary shell commands.
- Verify that other hook/policy denials still win and that the rewrite does not widen shell authority.
- Inject SessionStart context showing the canonical simple recovery command so agents do not need compound forms.

Support the normal `deft` / `directive` forms and the repository's canonical `task ... -- ...` forwarding form explicitly. Other wrappers must pass `--session-id` or `DEFT_SESSION_ID` themselves.

No host-to-lease binding file is introduced.

### 3. Align lease, ritual, and host identity

In the dispatcher:

- Pass canonical host identity to the occupancy write gate.
- Preserve explicit/environment conflict detection instead of letting a stale variable override the payload.
- After ritual verification, compare the verified ritual owner ID with the live lease and host ID.
- Add distinct diagnostics for identity unavailable, identity conflict, and lease/ritual mismatch.

Do **not** independently re-read ritual state after verification. The verifier currently reloads and can rewrite state during gated checks. A post-verification read creates this race:

1. Hook A verifies ritual A.
2. Session B steals and writes lease/ritual B.
3. Hook A re-reads ritual B.
4. Hook A can be mistaken for B.

Expose the session ID from the exact state the verifier evaluated through an internal result/helper. Keep it out of public `verify:session-ritual --json` output.

A matching but stale ritual should still result in `ritual-not-ready`, not `occupancy-occupied`; freshness and actor alignment remain separate gates.

### 4. Resolve lifecycle identity once and carry it end to end

For each lifecycle invocation, resolve one session ID and carry it through preview, claim, nested calls, persistence, and output. Do not call a minting resolver independently at each stage.

`session:ready` specifically must carry the ID through its whole state machine:

- Initial occupancy preview.
- Any nested `session:start`.
- Gated verification.
- Final occupancy claim.
- Capture the ID produced by a successful nested cold start rather than minting again.

Include `swarm:launch`: the merged occupancy-before-worktree path at `packages/core/src/swarm/launch.ts:1080-1083` still supplies environment only. After an unpinned host session claims occupancy, launch can mint a foreign UUID and self-deny before worktree creation. Thread the explicit host ID into launch; keep its existing failure cleanup using the returned occupancy ID.

Keep `releaseSwarmOccupancy` manifest/cohort based. Ritual fallback could release the wrong cohort and is not needed when launch records the canonical owner ID.

### 5. Fix steal and migration transitions

A second source-level defect changes the recovery plan: `session:start --steal` currently steals twice.

- Preview uses `write=true` when `steal` is set.
- Persistence invokes the same steal-shaped operation again.
- The second invocation still names the old occupant, which no longer matches the newly written owner.

Fix this in #3611 because confirmed steal is the supported migration/recovery path:

1. Resolve the incoming canonical host ID once.
2. Validate the named occupant without mutating during preview.
3. Perform one confirmed steal.
4. Complete ritual persistence with the same ID.
5. Use ordinary same-ID claim/heartbeat behavior afterward, not a second steal.
6. If later ceremony persistence fails, clean up or leave an explicit fail-closed mismatch with deterministic rerun recovery.

Existing UUID-based live leases cannot automatically become host-namespaced owners. Migration must be explicit and idempotent:

- Preferred: rewritten `session:start --steal --confirm --occupant <old-id> --session-id=<host-id>` aligns lease and ritual.
- Bare `occupancy:steal` is lease-only. Its success output must state that writes remain denied until `session:start --rearm` aligns ritual state.
- Remove bare steal from the normal one-step remediation text.
- Raw deletion of `.deft/occupancy.json`, if documented at all, is emergency administrative cleanup that disables occupancy protection; it is not the normal recovery.

Intermediate lease/ritual mismatch is expected to deny. File-based gating cannot make the two-file transition transactional, but it can make it fail closed and rerunnable under the cooperative model.

### 6. Expanded regression plan

Add host-shaped fixtures and a real multi-process lifecycle test:

1. Feed a SessionStart/PreToolUse lifecycle command with host identity A.
2. Assert the renderer rewrites the exact command with canonical owner A.
3. Execute the rewritten command in a separate child process with `DEFT_SESSION_ID` removed.
4. Assert lease and ritual both contain canonical A.
5. Invoke the built direct-write hook in another child with payload A and no environment ID; assert allow from rendered stdout.
6. Invoke it with payload B; assert `occupancy-occupied`/identity denial.
7. Invoke it without usable payload identity; assert fail-closed denial.
8. Assert no binding/credential file was created.

Both hook allow and deny decisions exit status `0`; tests must parse rendered host output, not use process status as the verdict.

Additional required cases:

- Payload identity and environment identity conflict.
- Codex parent and subagent events share the intended session-family owner.
- Claude session plus `agent_id` still uses the session-family key.
- Cursor concurrent conversations differ; live-confirm Cursor parent/subagent behavior before claiming family semantics.
- Exact lifecycle command rewrite versus compound/ambiguous command refusal.
- Rewrite does not bypass an independent hook/policy denial.
- Matching stale ritual reports `ritual-not-ready`.
- Verified-state ownership transition A→B cannot let old hook A proceed.
- `session:ready` with initially missing ritual does not mint preview/start/final IDs independently.
- `session:start --steal` performs one steal and leaves matching lease/ritual.
- Bare steal produces mismatch denial plus actionable recovery.
- `swarm:launch` reuses canonical A and explicit foreign B denies before worktree creation.
- `occupancy:release`/`session:end` works with canonical A and rejects B.
- POSIX and Windows child invocation is shell-independent; use explicit CLI args rather than shell environment-prefix syntax.
- Production ritual fixture satisfies live hook-readiness verification; do not hide the lifetime bug behind an in-process mocked verifier.

### 7. Documentation and rollout delta

Update all consumer-visible ownership surfaces, not only `content/commands.md`:

- `formatOccupancyRemediation` and ritual recovery copy.
- CLI help and `tasks/occupancy.yml`.
- `AGENTS.md` and `content/templates/agents-entry.md` together, followed by `task agents:refresh` per #1309.
- Swarm launch/close-out copy.
- Hook fixture documentation.
- `CHANGELOG.md`.

State explicitly:

- This is cooperative host-session routing, not same-user authentication.
- Codex owner granularity includes parent and subagents.
- Missing/drifted hooks remain #3742.
- Spawn occupancy bypass remains #3755.
- #3611 alone does not renew the 20-minute heartbeat; #3599 remains the immediate follow-up.

## Revised acceptance criteria

1. A standard host-mediated mutation ceremony claims lease and writes ritual using the same canonical host session ID without relying on inherited `DEFT_SESSION_ID`.
2. A later direct-write hook from the same host session is allowed with no environment ID.
3. A different concurrent host conversation is denied even when both can read the same worktree ritual state.
4. Missing, malformed, or conflicting payload identity fails closed when a live lease exists.
5. The exact verified ritual owner, live lease owner, and canonical host owner must agree; mismatch never allows a write.
6. No persisted host-to-lease map, credential artifact, occupancy-derived caller identity, or schema migration is introduced.
7. Rearm, ready, release/end, confirmed steal, and swarm launch carry one resolved identity through their full state machines.
8. Confirmed `session:start --steal` steals once and establishes matching lease/ritual state; bare steal has explicit mismatch recovery.
9. Real child-process tests cover claim and later hook lifetimes on host-shaped payloads and parse the rendered verdict.
10. Existing expiry, locking/fencing, read-only, scope, runtime, assist-scratch, and separately tracked spawn behavior is preserved.

Still keep this as one atomic PR after the issue/xBRIEF contract is recut and explicitly approved. #3599 follows immediately. #3729, #3742, #3754, and #3755 remain separate.

This amendment supersedes the ritual-as-actor portions of [the earlier plan](https://github.com/deftai/directive/issues/3611#issuecomment-5424890479); its process gates, atomic-PR requirement, no-security-boundary statement, and general verification discipline remain valid.
